title: A monthly close checklist in formulas

docs.syntax: =IF(variance=0,"ready","check") flags one check; =COUNTIF(range,"<>0") counts the rest
docs.explain:
IF tests a condition and returns one of two values, so a checklist row can answer in words. The formula =IF(B2=0,"ready","check") reads the variance and gives ready at zero, check at anything else. Four variances can be read by eye; forty cannot.

The bank row sits at zero, so it reads ready, and so does payroll. Accruals at 12.5 and prepaids at -3 come back as check. The second screen counts the rows still out with COUNTIF(B2:B5,"<>0"), and the answer is 2.

The criterion goes in quotes because a comparison is written as text. COUNTIF reads <>0 as not equal to the number 0. Drop the third argument and the failing row shows FALSE, which reads as a fault in the formula. Both outcomes belong in the call.

errors.text: A variance is divided by zero before the comparison is made.
The function is typed as IF or COUNTIF with a letter missing, so Excel finds nothing to run.
The two branches are swapped, so a variance of zero reads check.

docs.atWork: Turning a column of close variances into a ready or check flag, then counting the rest.
docs.outcome: Flag a reconciliation from its variance, then count the rows still out.
docs.teaches: IF returning a word instead of a number, then COUNTIF with a not-equal criterion
docs.dataset: Four close reconciliations, each with a variance to judge

screens.prompt: In C2, flag the first reconciliation ready when its variance is zero and check otherwise.

hints.syntax: =IF(B2=0,"ready","check"): the test, then the word for each outcome.
hints.func-if: One cell has to choose between two words, which is IF's work.
hints.value: The bank variance is zero, so the status reads ready.
hints.error: Divide the variance by zero and the grader reports an error before either word appears.

screens.prompt: In C2, count the reconciliations whose variance is not zero.

hints.syntax: =COUNTIF(B2:B5,"<>0"): the variance column, then the quoted criterion.
hints.func-countif: Counting rows that meet a condition is what COUNTIF does.
hints.value: Accruals and prepaids are out, so the count is two.
hints.error: A formula that divides by zero is what the grader's error rule catches here.

seo.title: A close checklist built from IF and COUNTIF
seo.description: IF returns ready or check for one variance, and COUNTIF with a quoted not-equal criterion counts the rows still out. No line needs reading by eye.
